Reddit announces two upcoming changes that may upset some long-time users.

The company has already placed a restriction on old Reddit, and is now announcing a second. Additionally, RSS support will be discontinued…

Old Reddit

Reddit significantly redesigned its user interface back in 2018, which drew strong backlash from users who preferred the old version. In response to those voices, the platform promised at the time that as long as people were still using it, they would continue to offer what later became known as "old Reddit."

This past August, the company changed this policy for the first time, requiring users of old Reddit to be logged in. Now they are announcing again that the old interface will only be available to users who have used it within the past six months, and new users will not be able to access it.

Reddit says both measures are intended to reduce the company's AI scraping (though if you're willing to pay for a license, the issue apparently no longer exists).

RSS Feed Support Ending

The discontinuation of RSS feed support is also based on the same reasoning.

For subreddits that rely on RSS to maintain their moderation workflow, this change could have a particularly large impact. Reddit says they are aware of this situation and suggests moderators switch to Devvit apps, such as Discord Relay.

Users react coolly

A look at the comments section shows that many long-time users are very unhappy with these latest developments.

What are your thoughts on these latest changes? Feel free to share them in the comments.
